title: Gestureless cost & rollout controls: keyboard-first interactions and color-delta contrast audit
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Several Console surfaces (compact Cost Explorer cards and Rollouts inspector) rely on hover-only affordances and color-deltas that become inaccessible for keyboard-only users and fragile across locales and high-contrast themes. This ticket prototypes a "gestureless" interaction model: all critical actions (inspect, promote, rollback, pin-to-favorites, per-route cost breakdown) must be operable via keyboard-only focus and persistent, non-hover-dependent controls while preserving a compact density for metric-dense dashboards. Additionally, perform a color-delta audit to ensure WCAG 2.1 AA contrast delta is preserved when dynamic theme or locale number formatting changes color/weight of tokens.
acceptance_criteria: All actionable controls on compact cost cards and rollout rows reachable and operable via keyboard without requiring hover
No functionality is hidden behind hover-only popovers; tooltips converted to ARIA-friendly anchors or inline toggles where appropriate
Color-delta mapping documented and implemented so token contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA across themes and with localized numeric glyphs (e.g., non-Latin digits)
Prototype validated in usability test with at least 6 keyboard-only participants showing >=90% task success for: opening rollout details, promoting a canary, and viewing per-route cost breakdown
Engineering implementation plan (ENG owners assigned) and perf impact <5% DOM increase for pages with 100+ cost cards
engineering_feedback: ENG: large-scale persistent controls increase DOM size; propose virtualization + progressive enhancement to only hydrate actions for visible viewport (ENG-8812)
ENG: suggest using aria-controls + aria-expanded patterns instead of replicating full popover content (reduces JS work)
ENG: color-delta tokens should map to existing theme token system; avoid introducing bespoke CSS variables for each component (cross-platform maintenance cost)
ENG: i18n team flagged numeral width differences (Devanagari, Arabic-Indic) that affect perceived contrast — recommend testing with realistic glyph sets (ENG-8890)
usability_test_notes: Session: 6 keyboard-only participants (mix of screenreader users and sighted keyboard users)
Finding: Hover-only context menus were unreachable by 5/6 participants; switching to persistent mini-toolbar inside card solved the flow
Finding: Focus order in dense grids required explicit tab stops; users expected arrow-key movement in card grids — design decision needed
Suggestion: Add visible focus ring with 3px minimum contrast delta from background to meet perception thresholds for low-vision users
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Use minimal persistent action strip (three icons) visible on focus and on non-hover touch as default; avoids always-on visual clutter while remaining keyboard-accessible
Tradeoff: Slightly larger card chrome vs completely hidden actions; accepted to meet keyboard and screenreader expectations
Decision: Keep rich details in collapsible inline panels rather than full-screen modal to reduce context switching and preserve reading flow for screenreader users
Tradeoff: Inline panels add DOM nodes; will mitigate with virtualization and lazy hydration
accessibility_checks: WCAG contrast pass for normal text and icons across light/dark/high-contrast themes
Keyboard: all controls reachable via Tab and operable via Enter/Space; arrow-key navigation proposal documented for later sprint
Screenreader: ARIA labels for action strip, descriptive aria-describedby for dynamic cost deltas
I18n: verify number formatting and token wrapping in RTL and wide-digit locales; ensure truncation rules maintain semantic clarity
reviews: PM review (Samira Chen): requested metric on rollback success rate to be instrumented
Accessibility review (Liam O'Neill): approved color-delta mapping but asked for contrast tests against simulated low-vision filters
Engineering review (Priya Rao): accepted approach with virtualization caveat; ENG-8812 owner assigned

Create ENG spike for virtualization + lazy-hydration (ENG-8812) — owner: Miguel Ortega — due 2026-03-18
